conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced turned up: IBM's own Q3 guide (cc growth in line with the 4-5% FY range, 1.5pt FX headwind) puts its stated low-end base case at about $16.74bn, below a $16.84bn consensus; the memory-price driver of the Q2 deferrals was still running in Q3; and the stock has run +7.4% in five sessions into a print it has usually sold. Against that, a third of the slipped deals closed in July and Accenture's bookings beat. So p_up 45 on a 7.5% abs move gives -0.75. impact_sum (-1.1) is a little larger than the scaled number because it carries the positioning item at full size, while p_up holds it as a lean only.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus $16.84bn / EPS $2.87 (Zacks) and $16.85bn / $2.89 (Benzinga), two agreeing sources per https://finviz.com/news/399932/ibm-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results search summary and https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/evercore-isi-reiterates-ibm-stock-rating-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4958419 (Evercore cites $16.8bn / $2.86). Company guide from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15273247436645376): Q3 cc revenue growth consistent with the FY 4-5% (low end called the base case), currency a 1.5pt headwind, Q3 operating pre-tax margin similar to Q2. On the Q3 2025 base of $16.33bn (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/ibm-q2-2026-earnings) that implies about $16.74-16.90bn reported. Consensus sits inside the guided range, above its low end. FY: cc revenue +4-5%, software +6-8%, FCF +~$1bn, +100bp operating pre-tax margin. Evercore puts the Q4 bar at $20.5bn / $4.58 vs a $4.62 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest 33.1M shares, 2.2 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement, per https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ibm/short-interest/. Equibles shows about 2.36% of float and 1.8 days, undated (https://equibles.com/stocks/ibm/shortinterest). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. Baseline 25d skew is -0.65 vol points, balanced; put/call OI is 0.61, call-heavy. Event-implied move 6.76%; TipRanks quotes 7.16%. Run-up: +7.42% over 5 days and +5.17% over 20, from $226.61 on Oct 8 (https://site.financialmodelingprep.com/market-news/ibm-stock-analysis-price-target-earnings-outlook) to $244.79 at the seal. The stock is still -25.7% from its 52-week high after the -25.2% day on 2026-07-14.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus ($16.84-16.85bn) sits above IBM's own stated base case for the quarter. On the Q2 call (2026-07-22) management guided Q3 constant-currency growth 'consistent with the full year' (4-5%, low end the base case) with FX a 1.5pt headwind. On the Q3 2025 base of $16.33bn that gives about $16.74bn at the low end and $16.90bn at the high. The Street is therefore pricing roughly the upper half of the guide, on a company that missed revenue by about $0.66bn last quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue miss ($17.16bn vs ~$17.5-17.9bn): -25.2% on the pre-announcement (2026-07-14), then +0.43% on the full print. Q1 2026 beat: -8.25%. Q3 2025 beat ($16.33bn, +9%): -0.87%. IBM has repeatedly sold revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is public, but the consensus sits about $0.1bn above the low end that management called its base case. If the market had marked to the base case, revenue estimates would read about $16.74bn rather than $16.84bn. Evercore expects 'in line to slightly better', which shows the Street is anchored above the low end.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 revenue base from https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/ibm-q2-2026-earnings. Consensus from Zacks and Benzinga via https://finviz.com/news/399932/ibm-to-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results. UBS's $16.68bn estimate (cited at https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220955-ibm-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-deal-recovery-238-breakout-october-16-2026-tradingkey) points the same way. This finding shares the transcript with the slipped-deals finding below.

findings.finding: The driver IBM blamed for the Q2 software and ELA deferrals did not stop in Q3. TrendForce (2026-07-03) forecast conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in 3Q26, with server DRAM still undersupplied, though rising more slowly than in prior quarters. IBM said the low end of its 6-8% FY software range 'assumes that recent spending dynamics persist through the second half', so this proxy points to the low end of the software range in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-14 pre-announcement, which attributed the miss to client capex shifting to servers, storage and memory: -25.2%. The full Q2 print a week later: +0.43%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, since the memory story is well known. But the Street's focus, per Evercore, is on deferral 'rather than destruction' and on slipped deals converting in Q3. Continued price increases mean the incentive to pull budget toward hardware persisted through the quarter. If this were priced, the consensus would sit at the guide's low end.
findings.independence: Proxy only; neither IBM nor a direct counterparty has confirmed it for Q3. The moderation in price increases (https://www.igorslab.de/en/dram-and-nand-remain-more-expensive-trendforce-sees-slowing-but-still-rising-memory-prices-q3-2026/) cuts the other way, which is why the size is small. The offset elsewhere in the company: IBM Distributed Infrastructure (Power and Storage, +37% in Q2 with a ~$500M backlog) benefits from the same shift.

findings.finding: Slipped-deal recapture is on company record. On the Q2 call Krishna said 'about a third' of the large deals that slipped from Q2 closed in the first few weeks of Q3, and that he would normally expect 'two-thirds to three-quarters of them to close over the next six months'. That transactional software revenue should land in Q3, against a quarter the company guided only to the FY growth rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The full Q2 print carrying this commentary rose +0.43% after the -25% pre-announcement, so the market gave it little credit.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July and mostly priced. UBS reads the recapture as 'less than half', and the Street still sits inside the guide rather than above it. If the market believed the recapture plus normal Q3 flow, Q3 software estimates would be above the 6-8% FY run-rate. What is left unpriced is whether the remaining two-thirds also closed by September.
findings.independence: Fox Business interview, 2026-07-23 (https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/ibm-ceo-addresses-wall-street-tech-panic-after-delayed-enterprise-software-deals-surge-back): same claim, same speaker, so not independent. Evercore's 2026-10-19 note names this as the key question (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/evercore-isi-reiterates-ibm-stock-rating-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4958419). Shares the transcript with finding 1.

findings.finding: Accenture, a consulting peer reporting after IBM last spoke, posted strong numbers on 2026-10-01 for the quarter ended Aug 31: new bookings $22.2bn (+4% USD, +5% LC) against roughly $19.9bn expected, consulting revenue $9.28bn (+6%), consulting bookings $9.40bn, and an FY27 revenue outlook above the Street. That points to IBM Consulting ($5.3bn, flat in Q2) at least holding its guided 'low to mid single digit' acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IBM rose about 2.6% on the day of Accenture's release, its largest gain since September. Consulting has rarely been the line IBM's stock trades on; software and Z dominate.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: IBM moved +2.6% on the day. IBM Consulting estimates may not have been raised, since previews do not mention consulting at all. If they had been, previews would flag consulting upside.
findings.independence: TCS Q2 FY27 (about 2026-10-09): TCV $9.6bn and stock +5.5% (https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/tcs-share-price-jumps-5-46-after-q2-fy27-results-net-profit-rises-4-qoq-to-13884-crore). Indian IT previews still describe discretionary spend as weak (https://www.bajajbroking.in/share-market-news/it-q2-fy27-preview-tcs-infosys-growth-seen-as-muted).

findings.finding: IBM rose about 8% from $226.61 on 2026-10-08 to $244.79 at today's seal (+7.42% over 5 sessions), with no IBM-specific release found to explain the last week. That takes it to roughly the $250 targets of the two most bullish previewers (Evercore, JPMorgan), into a print whose stock has fallen after 5 of its last 8 reports, including 'beats'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline last 8 reactions: +0.43, -25.21 (pre-announcement), -8.25, +5.13, -0.87, -7.62, -6.58, +12.96; 3 up. The Q3 2025 beat with a raised guide drew -0.87%.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew is balanced (-0.65 vol points) and put/call OI is 0.61, call-heavy, so options are not positioned for a give-back. If the run-up were seen as stretched, puts would be bid. With the price at the bull targets, an in-line quarter has less room to rally.
findings.independence: Evercore $250 target (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/evercore-isi-reiterates-ibm-stock-rating-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4958419); Morgan Stanley raised to $238, Equal-Weight (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262220955-ibm-stock-forecast-q3-earnings-deal-recovery-238-breakout-october-16-2026-tradingkey). Both are below or at spot.

findings.finding: IBM Z faces its hardest comparison of the cycle. Q3 2025 Z revenue grew 59-61% YoY ('highest Q3 revenue in nearly two decades') and lifted Infrastructure 17%. Q2 2026 Z was already -42%, so Infrastructure (~$3.8bn) likely prints a deep Z decline again. Netted against Distributed Infrastructure, which grew 37% with a ~$500M backlog exiting Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Z -42% in Q2 2026 was part of the -25% pre-announcement. The +61% Z quarter (Q3 2025) drew -0.87%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the comparison is public and Q2 already showed the decline. The residual is that management guided FY Infrastructure to 'grow low single digits' on 'high 120% plus program-to-program' Z, which requires a strong H2 that the comparison makes hard to show.

findings.finding: IBM lost a major services contract with the IRS. The agency did not renew it, and about 100 jobs at IBM's Rocket Center, WV site were cut, effective 2026-09-04 (WCBC, 2026-08-27). It is a small consulting/services revenue hole starting late in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history; IBM's stock has not moved on single federal contracts.
findings.why_not_priced: Local news, not covered in any preview. Immaterial against $5.3bn of quarterly consulting.

findings.finding: FX looks roughly as guided. A NAGA Q3 2026 FX review puts DXY about +0.2% over Q3 (low 98.79 on Sep 8, 102.54 by Oct 5), with EUR/USD -0.3%, so there is no sign the dollar moved enough to change the 1.5pt Q3 headwind IBM guided in July. The column labels in that table are ambiguous, so the source is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: IBM's stock has not reacted to FX in the reactions on record.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Q3 review; exact day not on page)
findings.why_not_priced: Neutral; recorded so the panel can see the FX assumption was checked.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced and does not argue either way. The slight negative lean here (consensus above IBM's base case, memory headwind persisting, the run-up into a name that sells prints) cuts against the +7.4% five-day run-up. Short interest is not crowded, so no squeeze offsets the negative.
lessons_applied: Consensus-vs-base-case finding shrunk -0.8 to -0.5: the consensus sits inside IBM's own guided 4-5% range, and a finding inside the guided range moves toward 0 (lesson 6).
Memory-price proxy shrunk -0.6 to -0.5: macro-to-company transmission IBM has not confirmed for Q3 is filed small (lesson 5).
Run-up/positioning shrunk -1.0 to -0.8: partly the same reaction-history concern as lesson 1 already held in p_up, and kept from stacking.
Z comparison netted against Distributed Infrastructure growth, -0.3 to -0.2 (lesson 9, segment net of the rest).
Accenture peer print kept at +0.5: a peer printing after the company last spoke is the kind of finding that has paid, but IBM already rose 2.6% on it.
